anya: FYI I'm opening a docs PR that tightens the Private installer preflight and adds explicit nftables + iptables examples for preserving client IP to HSMs. Noticed confusion in support tickets where gateway SNAT hides caller IP and breaks HSM audit logs.

kevin: thanks. Can you drop the exact firewall snippets here so I can sanity-check with infra? We want both a minimal iptables and an nft version.

anya: sure. iptables example (keep host-network->HSM exempt from MASQUERADE): ```sh
# only masquerade general egress, but exempt HSM subnet
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -m comment --comment "egress-masq" -j MASQUERADE
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.12.0.0/16 -d 172.16.50.0/24 -j RETURN
``` nftables alternative: ```nft
table ip nat {
  chain postrouting {
    type nat hook postrouting priority 100;
    oifname "eth0" masquerade comment "egress-masq"
    ip saddr 10.12.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.16.50.0/24 accept
  }
}
```

li: small note 1	RETURN in iptables is fine but clarify that it must come before a general MASQUERADE rule if you show them in the same chain. For nft I would show the specific accept rule above the masquerade so order is obvious.

anya: good catch, reordered the examples in the PR and added inline comments about rule ordering.

docs-bot: PR #2180 opened by anya 1	docs/private/installer/preflight.md 1	reviewers: kevin, li

kevin: also include a preflight snippet to validate forwarding, NAT rules and cert-validity clock skew. People forget to check host time on sealed installs.

anya: added this preflight checklist to the PR: ```sh
# preflight checks
sysctl -n net.ipv4.ip_forward || echo "ERROR: ip_forward disabled"
# ensure a route exists to HSM (example HSM IP 172.16.50.10)
ip route get 172.16.50.10 || echo "WARN: no route to HSM"
# nftables/iptables quick checks
iptables -t nat -S | grep -E "MASQUERADE|RETURN" || true
nft list ruleset | grep -E "masquerade|postrouting" || true
# verify clock not skewed (HSM certs are strict)
date -u && timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized
```

li: for air-gapped customers mention chrony with local fallback and avoid default public pool configs. Maybe add a tiny chrony snippet that points to local NTP appliance.

anya: added a short chrony example and a one-line note: "If fully isolated, point to on-prem NTP server(s) and do not configure public NTP pools."

kevin: can you also add an SDK example? Ops usually want a concrete client snippet showing TLS client cert usage. Prefer a Go example since most infra teams use Go.

anya: added this Go snippet in the PR comments: ```go
import (
  "github.com/redwood/redwood-go-sdk"
)
client, _ := redwood.NewPrivateClient(redwood.ClientOptions{
  KMSEndpoint: "https://kms.internal.local:8443",
  TLSCert:     "/etc/pki/client.crt",
  TLSKey:      "/etc/pki/client.key",
  CACert:      "/etc/pki/ca.crt",
})
// ensure the client cert's CN maps to an HSM principal
_ = client.Healthcheck()
```

li: looks good. Suggest renaming TLSCert/TLSKey keys to client_cert and client_key in the example to match our SDK parameter docs. Small editorial.

anya: updated to client_cert/client_key.

kevin: one more thing 1	add a short test harness script people can run locally to emulate a bridged HSM and validate the preflight. Keeps support tickets down.

anya: added test-hsm-setup.sh: ```sh
# quick local test: creates netns and bridges to simulate gateway
sudo ip netns add hsmtest
sudo ip link add veth-host type veth peer name veth-ns
sudo ip link set veth-ns netns hsmtest
sudo ip addr add 10.12.0.1/24 dev veth-host
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest ip addr add 10.12.0.2/24 dev veth-ns
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest ip route add default via 10.12.0.1
# run curl from namespace against host-local HSM emulator
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest curl -v https://172.16.50.10:8443/health --resolve "172.16.50.10:8443:172.16.50.10" --cert client.crt --key client.key
```
